Dialogue Text

column3: This is the first real interaction with MARCO
column4: Siri… what’s the date?

column3: First time responding - Kim has called you Siri
column4: This is Marco, your personal assistant app!
Right. Marco. Whatever.
It’s not really a case of ‘whatever’. I’m the most advanced AI that’s been devised. I don’t even rely on wifi, which is pretty useful given where you’ve found yourself.
Where have I…

I’m only bringing it up because – got to address it, elephant in the room – I did hear you say earlier that I was a, quote, ‘shitty version of Siri’. I realise this was ignorance rather than malice, but of course, it hurts. I’m many more times more powerful than Siri, Alex, any of these goons.
Fine. I didn’t mean to… like, I wouldn’t think it would be possible to hurt the feelings of a…

Of a machine. No. My super-intelligence is both blessing and curse. Anyway, what was it you wanted to ask? Another thing about my sophisticated human mimicry is that I quite often forget what the hell I’m meant to be doing.
I was asking you what date it is, what… what year it is.
Oh. Easy. It’s August 5th... \. 1526.

column4: Dialogue Text

column3: [Kim just helped Alice barely squeeze onto the train]
column4: Oh my God, <b>thank you!
Hey, does this go to Stockwell?
Um, No.
Oh. Probably shouldn’t have risked my life getting on.
But you could actually change at – well, stay on and I’ll show you.
Thank you! You live in London?
Um. Yep
You’re welcome…
Dialogue Text
Is that your uniform? I mean, I guess it is.\nYou probably wouldn’t wear a name badge if it was your real clothes.
Yes, I work at – um. I’ve just started at, do you know the Bankside Museum!
Cool, yeah!
Do you know it?
Um. No. I just wanted to sound enthusiastic.
(Laughter) Fair enough
I’ve been to London Zoo if that’s the same kind of thing?
I guess it is, yeah.
It’s not, remotely, is it?
I mean, no. We don’t have any live animals. \nThey don’t have any 16th century tableware.
Dialogue Text
So you don’t live in London?
I don’t live anywhere. I’m homeless!
…what?
God sorry, that was a stupid joke. Um I just mean I don’t have a home – a specific home – right now. I’m on my way to look at a place. A house share.
Oh right. Well, I – I hope it works out.
Me too, or I might end up sleeping in the museum after you lock up.
Um, I don’t think…
Another stupid joke! Sorry again. I – sometimes I do that when I’m nervous.
What are you nervous about, about the… house…
I just mean about, you know, whether I like the house.
Oh! This is you
Dialogue Text
Good Luck!
Dialogue Text
Excuse me, can I ask you a question?
Of course! It’s beautiful, isn’t it? Probably late Medieval. What would you like to know?
Where are the toilets?
Oh. Um. Down that way, first on the right.
Dialogue Text
Hey, I had a question too
Oh! – hey!
Hey, we met on the…
I remember, yes. So – what was your question? Let me guess: toilets or gift shop.
Wrong
Oh!
Dialogue Text
…that’s the thing, history isn’t something that’s finished, gone. It’s forever. We’re part of it right now, we take our little turn.
There are things even in this room that were around long before we were born and will still be here after we’re dead.
Dialogue Text
Damn it, I thought we were going to get through one without anyone crying. OK… any questions?
Dialogue Text
Have you ever been locked in here at night and like all the mummies and the dinosaurs come to life and you have to kill them before they kill you?
Haha, no, I’ve been here a few years now and I’ve never been threatened by anyone from the undead. Anyone else?<waitfor=1>yes?
If you did have to try and kill a mummy, what weapon would you…
Has anyone got a question that isn’t about the museum turning into a horror movie?
OK, well, thanks for coming to the Bankside Museum. If you’d like to leave a review… <waitfor=1> Oh, sorry. Miss Crane was it?
Yes. Sorry, this might sound silly, but do you think time travel will ever be possible? Or has ever been possible. If you see what I mean.
Well. Good question. I guess the argument against it is – you’ve probably heard of the time travel paradox.
And in that version of the world we might not be here to go back and change that thing. So, I guess I’d say…
Miss, Miss, Donny’s got a nosebleed and it’s gone on a vase.
If we could go back and change even the smallest thing, we’d create a different world.
Dialogue Text
waaah...
Dialogue Text
I was going to ask if you have a café.
(sighs) We do, but they’ll be closing, they normally close at…
OK, how about a pub?
What? We’re a museum, we…
You’re not making this easy. Can I take you to the pub?
For a drink?
When you finish work?
…oh.
It’s Alice, by the way. You can say no, I don’t even know if you’re… I just had to ask. And I was passing anyway.
<pause> Were you?
No. It took me an hour and a quarter to get here.
I’m Kim. And… yes please.
Dialogue Text
Yes, you.
Dialogue Text
GOOD DAY TO YE! LET US TALK!
So, this app supposedly – they gave a free trial to everyone at the museum – they claim it can translate between modern and ancient languages. I’ve literally never opened it.
We don’t get a lot of Ancient Mesopotamians coming round. Lucky really, they might want some of their stuff back.
Dialogue Text
Good afternoon, how may I enlighten you?

This is basically like a tiny little Wikipedia for history stuff. Anything covered in the museum, you can find on here somewhere. Kind of makes it pointless me having spent years learning it all, I guess, but there we go.
Dialogue Text
Yeah, I’d rather not look at that right now. It’s – it just reminds you about birthdays, appointments, whatever. But today is… well. I’m not likely to forget.
Dialogue Text

Mobile AI Research Companion and Organiser. This is just like a shitty version of Siri. I pretty much never use it. There are aspects of my existence I’d like to subcontract to a robot, but thinking – not so much.
Dialogue Text
Madame, with the greatest respect, should I take one of the menus away?
Dialogue Text
FOUND YOU!
What are you doing!?
Um, just being a legend at hide and seek?
Chloe’s meant to be seeking! You know, the one whose eighth birthday it is?
Well your niece is shit at finding people and I was missing you.
Dialogue Text
OK gently… gently… and go for it…
Dialogue Text
[panel=4]God this is so embarrassing, can you come and find me?
I thought you were standing me up! On a first date!
[panel=4]No, I’m just an idiot
OK, what can you see?
[panel=4]Um. Grass.
…right, I'll just look around London for some grass.
Dialogue Text
Ok, I think thats enough of that
Dialogue Text
Hey – shall we get married?
Oh my god, you meant it!
Because you can’t live without my amazing hand-eye coordination?
Ha Ha Ha...

Hello campers! It’s 4pm, we’re skipping off school early, it’s time to pack and hit the road!
I can’t believe this, I can’t believe you’ve talked me into this.
Do you mean ‘hi Christian, I can’t wait for our weekend camping adventure’?
I must have had some sort of brain injury.
I’m sure you’re not conscious of this, Kimbo, but you’re almost sounding a bit negative about the trip.
I mean why would I go on holiday to a place that’s worse than my actual flat? Isn’t the point of a holiday –
We’ve covered this, the ‘point’ of a holiday is to spend time with your beloved best friend…
That’s you, is it?
Unless I’ve been demoted, yes – with your beloved best friend, getting a change of scene for the weekend.
do you still have some camping concerns?
Of course, Cris. I’m just being adorably grumpy.
I mean, is there a way of having a ‘change of scene’ where there’s also a proper toilet?
I – I am kind of having second thoughts
Ah, sorry, I missed the adorable bit
On the website it says the toilets have actually gone up from two to three stars.
Right. Any chance you could have THIRD thoughts?
Shut your face!
I’ll just hold on till we get home, I reckon. I’ve done 72 hours before.
(Sigh) Fine. I’ve had third thoughts and I’ll try not to have fourth ones in the next hour.
Consider it shut
They don’t just give those three-star awards away, you know
If you do, just text me and we’ll see if we can get you onto fifth thoughts
OK, so I’ll see you at mine in – what, two hours? Get to the site for like half past eight, it’ll still be light for us to put the tent up
Christ. I’d forgotten the tent aspect. Are you sure you wouldn’t rather go to a…
…and from now on I’m singing tunelessly over any further objections! La la la la la! La-la-la!
Remember. Two Hours. My Place. Campiiing!
End chat
